page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-4-lssd is a general-purpose server instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor running at 2.3 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled to deliver 2 threads per core. The processor is equipped with a substantial 504 MB L3 cache, alongside 48 KB L1d and 2 MB L2 caches. It includes 15 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 402 GB local NVMe SSD, though the instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-threaded capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core testing. Text processing performance is also in the top tier. However, multi-core performance is comparatively weaker, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into the bottom 25%. Memory read bandwidth is average, reaching 345.89 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 42.84 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, while large block write bandwidth is weaker at 23.42 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a balanced profile by combining dedicated Intel Xeon compute resources with high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. The inclusion of local storage reduces the need for external block storage attachments for temporary data. It is well-suited for workloads such as static web serving, database operations, and single-threaded data processing tasks. Conversely, it is less optimal for highly parallelized multi-threaded computations or medium-to-large language model inference, where text generation speeds drop significantly.
